title: Spiral galaxy NGC 1637
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 1637, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 1637, Supernova · constellation Eridanus · about 35 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: NGC 1637 is a spiral galaxy about 35 million light-years away, pictured here by ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile. It lies in the constellation Eridanus, the River.

NGC 1637 has its own place in the study of exploding stars. Scientists found a Type II supernova in the galaxy in 1999, and they went on to follow its slow fading over the years that followed. A Type II supernova is the explosion that ends the life of a massive star when its core collapses. Tracking how the light of such an event dims over time helps astronomers understand what happened to the star.
The image was made with the FORS1 instrument on the VLT, which observed the galaxy through blue, visual and red filters, together covering much of the range of light that human eyes can see.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.19 x 7.19 arcminutes) and distance (35 million light years), the frame spans roughly 73,000 × 73,000 light-years. Its light set out about 35 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS1 on the Very Large Telescope observed NGC 1637 in visible light through B, V and R filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The telescope's exposures gather far more light than an eye could.
